verdicts.reason: A drops the striped background to thin top and bottom strips, so the brand pattern is mostly lost. Its 48H badge is squashed into a flat ellipse floating under the box, and there is a large dead green gap above the CTA. B keeps the stripes, the box and the green panel in a clear top-to-bottom reading order; its only flaw is the small badge jammed into the top-left corner.

A is faithful to the original: stripes on top, a prominent box, then the green panel with a large headline and a strong CTA. Its only flaw is the cramped corner badge. In B the box is shrunk and the CTA is a tiny pill with barely readable text. B's 48H badge is squashed flat and pushed to the bottom over busy stripes, after the CTA, which breaks the reading order.

A keeps the product box as the hero above a well-ordered text panel. B shrinks the VOLTSTRIDE box to an illegible thumbnail at the very bottom, which reduces the key product image to almost nothing and puts it after the CTA. B's headline also breaks into four lines, leaving the panel top-heavy.

A keeps the box at a strong size, with the badge on the stripes as in the original; the badge is just cramped in the corner. B shrinks the box into a small top band. It also squashes the 48H badge into a skewed ellipse wedged between the body copy and the CTA, where it competes with the button and loses its shape.
